mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 3.0% compresses equity discount rates by reducing risk-free rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as capital shifts from fixed income to equities.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 3.0%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate decline exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals accelerating labor market strength, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings growth that drives positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE declines > 0.2pp, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in residential construction (HOUST > 1900) and consumer spending (RSAFS > 350000) indicates robust demand expansion, increasing corporate revenue visibility and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST>1900 and RSAFS>350000, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During industrial production contractions (INDPRO < 110), manufacturing supply chain disruptions intensify input costs and reduce corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when INDPRO < 110, or Rank IC > 0.05 in negative direction over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points within a month signals aggressive monetary tightening that immediately pressures equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp, or Rank IC < -0.04 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate below 4.5% consistently correlates with strong labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE < 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-consumer-spending regimes (RSAFS > 360000), retail sales growth accelerates, boosting corporate revenue forecasts and generating positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS > 360000, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous unemployment rate declines (UNRATE < 4.5%) and employment growth (PAYEMS > 135000) signal a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE<4.5 and PAYEMS>135000, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.
